hypotheses.claim: A rank-power monotone reshuffling of |removal_savings_i|/median(|savings|), gated multiplicatively by load-tightness, depot-distance and demand-share terms, will outperform the plain worst-cost removal (L3-ctrl) destroy policy on the heterogeneous-capacity dev_24 suite at 500 ms, because heterogeneous instances need stagnation-adaptive diversification (high p) rather than always-greedy removal (low p); the effect should be visible as a strictly lower mean tour length with the gain concentrated in high-demand-variance instances.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve score_ruin_nodes toward a multiplicative-gating + rank-power destroy rule: raw removal_savings_i normalized by a robust scale (median |savings|) then gated by load tightness (route_load/capacity), depot proximity (d(i,0)/mean depot dist), and demand share (demand_i/capacity), with the rank exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) increasing from ~0.7 (exploitative, low stagnation) to ~2.0 (diversifying, high stagnation) so early iterations remove high-savings-cost customers and stagnating iterations randomize the ruin set toward spatially dispersed, low-demand customers.
